scope.national_review_question: Across Medicare, how do coverage rules, payment values, cost sharing and administrative requirements affect access to clinically indicated care for women and men, including unequal effects of formally neutral rules?
scope.motivating_example_rule: Estradiol is one motivating case in a national review of drugs, procedures and care pathways; a single drug finding cannot establish or resolve the national question.
scope.medicare_benchmark_rule: Medicare is the national policy benchmark for care in later life and substantial health needs, not a claim that it finances most US care or that most lifetime care occurs after 65. Preserve younger Medicare beneficiaries separately. See research/medicare_benchmark.json for the rationale, age-stratification and measurement rules.
scope.topic_scope: Sex-specific conditions, conditions predominantly affecting one sex, and shared conditions across reproductive, sexual, cardiovascular, cancer, musculoskeletal, pain, mental health, preventive and rehabilitative care.
scope.comparison_rule: Use within-condition comparisons, clinically justified service groups and population-burden analyses. Do not require a direct counterpart for every sex-specific service. Consider utilization and service mix as possible mechanisms as well as confounders.
scope.policy_level_rule: Distinguish Original Medicare, Medicare Advantage and Part D; national rules, contractor decisions and plan implementation; preserve policy year and denominators.
scope.scope_decision: Exclude transgender-focused patient evidence and gender-affirming care from the present review and future white paper.
scope.mixed_population_rule: Use only separately extractable eligible cisgender male/female results from mixed-population studies. Exclude nonseparable mixed results from the primary synthesis and record the reason.
scope.unreported_identity_rule: Studies reporting only male/female remain candidate evidence pending full-text eligibility checks. Record gender identity as not reported; do not infer confirmed cisgender status or zero transgender participants.
scope.nonpatient_data_rule: Fee schedules, formularies and policy documents have no patient cohort. Retain when relevant to included indications and label as policy or code-level evidence.
scope.clinical_basis_rule: Separate shared body systems, female/male reproductive anatomy, female/male reproductive physiology and mixed or site-dependent services. Classify each indication rather than the molecule or assumed patient identity. Keep sex-defined eligibility and disease burden distinct. Classification details are in research/clinical_basis.json.
scope.anatomy_analysis_rule: Compare women and men within shared conditions when clinically comparable. For anatomy- or physiology-linked care, assess need, benefit and policy consistency without requiring an opposite-sex counterpart. Split bundled services by organ, indication and procedure before comparative synthesis.

scope.analysis_subject_rule: Code patient sex/gender and physician sex/gender separately for every study, with the unit of analysis and comparison axis. Keep patient care/access, service/anatomy valuation or coverage, physician sex/gender and general patient background distinct. These categories do not replace clinical-basis classification or eligibility screening.
scope.physician_evidence_rule: Physician-gender payment studies remain a separate contextual stream outside the primary patient-sex disparity synthesis. Distinguish annual collections, per-service payments, complete billing circumstances and salary; code-matched payment differences are not automatically identical-service differences. Clinician interview participants or prescriber data do not by themselves make a study a physician-gender comparison.
scope.interaction_evidence_rule: Code both patient and physician sex/gender when analyzed together; retain concordance or interaction results separately from each main effect. Never infer a patient-sex effect from a physician-gender comparison, a specialty label, or procedure anatomy.

evidenceSubjects.rule: Classify the analytic question separately from the source of data and the sex/gender of respondents. Keep patient sex/gender, patient anatomy or indication, and physician sex/gender distinct. Population-specific evidence is not automatically a between-sex comparison. 'Not extracted' marks limits of the current review rather than proof that a variable was absent from the original study.

benchmark.rationale: Use Medicare as a national policy benchmark for equitable access to clinically indicated care in later life, when chronic illness and per-person healthcare use are substantial. Compare coverage, payment and access with clinical need across shared systems and reproductive anatomy/physiology.
benchmark.age_rule: Emphasize later-life care without excluding younger Medicare beneficiaries. Analyze ages 65–74, 75–84 and 85+ when reported; distinguish under-65 beneficiaries and disability, ESRD or ALS entitlement where available. Preserve mixed-age studies with explicit applicability limits.
benchmark.measurement_rule: Separate per-person utilization, spending, unmet need and share of national spending. Cross-sectional age comparisons do not establish a lifetime share of care or isolate aging as the cause. Medicare enrollment is not an age variable, and Medicare policy is not a universal measure of clinical appropriateness.
benchmark.comparison_rule: For sex comparisons, retain age distribution, clinical need, severity, follow-up/person-time and mortality where available. Present crude and age-standardized or stratified results when justified. Prespecify adjustment for disease burden, disability and care setting; do not automatically remove potential mechanisms of inequity.
